full_judgment:
6. Mr Md Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, placed before us the judgment of the High Court Division and submits that the High Court Division failed to consider the case of the plaintiff-petitioners property and wrongly found that bonafide requirement was incidentally prayed for before the trial Court. 

 7. We have gone through the judgment of the High Court Division as well as of the trial Court. On perusal of the notice Exhibit 2 it is found that the same was addressed to the sons and daughter of Abdul Latif and both the notices were sent to said six persons but the High Court Division found that late Abdul Latif left behind sons, daughter and wife Tahera Khatun and this Tahera Khatun was named as defendant No. 7 but no notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was served upon her. It is well settled that without serving any notice under section 106 of the said Act no tenant can be evicted. The High Court Division considered this aspect of the matter and rightly made the Rule absolute. Mr Md Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, failed to point out any legal infirmity in the judgment of the High Court Division which may call for our interference.
